population_and_interval_notes: The historical Track A audit stores means and confidence intervals but not standard errors; its stored quantities are reconciled, while newly reconstructed standard errors are checked against the scheduler.
RMSE is root of mean origin/lead spatial MSE within each complete trajectory, then equal-weight trajectory mean.
Probability scores use qualified complete trajectories; point outcomes of unqualified native fits remain diagnostics.
Paired comparisons use exact shared complete trajectory IDs; incomplete cases are never imputed.
Finite extreme losses remain in scores. Full-schedule RMSE is undefined when any origin lacks a finite result.
VPT is a crossing of primary point-forecast error, not the distribution of individual predictive-path crossing times.
Aggregate scalar intervals use independent index-resampling with the prescribed seed and2000 draws and match the scheduler.

Historical A lead-audit intervals use index-resampling; the report figure renderer uses statistically equivalent multinomial trajectory weights, so those two finite Monte Carlo interval realizations need not be bitwise identical. This audit includes renderer-equivalent lead intervals as a separate reference.
Zero-event empirical bootstrap intervals describe observed clusters and do not establish zero new-trajectory failure probability.
Full predictive ensembles and model checkpoint arrays were not reread or regenerated; compact retained examples and receipt metadata were audited.
scope: Main A/B, primary seed only; sensitivity and contiguous results explicitly outside this completed audit
